hook.text: A cabochon is a domed, unfaceted stone.

lines.text: A cabochon is a domed, unfaceted stone.
It is shaped and polished into a smooth dome.
The back is usually flat, and the outline is usually an oval.
Opaque stones like opal and turquoise are usually cut this way.
Clear stones are usually faceted, like the diamonds in this ring.
A star sapphire needs the dome so the star can show.
A cat's eye stone shows its bright line across the dome.
The name comes from French, and the trade calls it a cab.
A garnet cut as a cabochon is called a carbuncle.
So a cabochon is a stone polished smooth, with no facets.
A render shows the setting and the stone before anything is cast.

post.caption: A cabochon is a gem polished into a smooth dome with no facets. The back is usually flat and the outline is usually an oval. Opaque stones like opal and turquoise are usually cut this way, while clear stones are usually faceted. A star sapphire needs the dome so the star shows, and a cat's eye stone shows a bright line across it. The name comes from French, and a garnet cut as a cabochon is called a carbuncle.
